Face

Face representation for Plot3D structured grid blocks.

This module defines the Face class, which represents a single face (quadrilateral or triangular surface) of a structured multi-block grid in the Plot3D format. A face is described by four (or three) corner vertices with spatial coordinates (x, y, z) and structured indices (I, J, K).

The class provides:

  • vertex-level geometry operations (centroid, normals, diagonal length),

  • index-range queries (IMIN … KMAX),

  • equality / hashing based on block index and index ranges,

  • polygon-based overlap detection (Sutherland-Hodgman clipping), and

  • node-sharing predicates for structured connectivity analysis.

class plot3d.face.Face(nvertex: int = 4)[source]

A face of a Plot3D structured grid block.

A face is bounded by four corner vertices (quad) or three (triangle) and carries both physical coordinates (x, y, z) and structured indices (I, J, K) for each vertex. The face may be I-constant, J-constant, or K-constant depending on which index is the same across all vertices.

__init__(nvertex: int = 4)[source]

Initialise a face with pre-allocated vertex storage.

Parameters:

nvertex – Maximum number of vertices (4 for a quad, 3 for a triangle). Storage is always allocated for 4 vertices regardless of this value.

copy() → Face[source]

Create an independent copy of this face.

Uses numpy.ndarray.copy for the coordinate and index arrays, which is significantly faster than copy.deepcopy.

Returns:

A new Face instance with identical attribute values.

to_dict() → Dict[str, int][source]

Return a dictionary representation of this face.

The dictionary keys are IMIN, JMIN, KMIN, IMAX, JMAX, KMAX, id, and block_index.

Returns:

A dictionary mapping string keys to integer values that fully describe the face’s index range and identity.

Centroid of the face as a length-3 array [cx, cy, cz].

Returns:

A NumPy array of shape (3,) with dtype float64.

Minimum I-index across all vertices.

Returns:

Returns:

property KMIN: int

Returns:

The smallest K value stored in this face.

property IMAX: int

Maximum I-index across all vertices.

Returns:

The largest I value stored in this face.

property JMAX: int

Maximum J-index across all vertices.

Maximum K-index across all vertices.

Returns:

property BlockIndex: int

Zero-based block index of the parent block.

Returns:

The block index as a Python int.

property const_type: int

Identify which structured index is constant across the face.

Returns:

0 if I-constant (IMIN == IMAX), 1 if J-constant (JMIN == JMAX), 2 if K-constant (KMIN == KMAX), or -1 if no single index is constant.

property isEdge: bool

Check whether the face degenerates to an edge.

A face is an edge when two or more of its three index ranges collapse (i.e., min equals max).

Returns:

True if the face degenerates to an edge, False otherwise.

property isPoint: bool

Check whether the face degenerates to a single point.

A face is a point when all three index ranges collapse.

Returns:

True if the face degenerates to a point, False otherwise.

get_val(i_val: int, j_val: int, k_val: int) → Tuple[float, float, float][source]

Retrieve the spatial coordinates for a specific vertex.

Searches the stored vertices for one whose (I, J, K) indices match the requested values exactly.

Parameters:

  • i_val – I-index of the desired vertex.

  • j_val – J-index of the desired vertex.

  • k_val – K-index of the desired vertex.

Returns:

A tuple (x, y, z) of the matching vertex coordinates.

Raises:

KeyError – If no vertex with the given (I, J, K) exists in this face.

add_vertex(x: float, y: float, z: float, i: int, j: int, k: int)[source]

Append a vertex to this face.

Vertices are stored in insertion order. Once the fourth vertex has been added the centroid (cx, cy, cz) is computed automatically as the mean of the four vertex positions.

Parameters:

  • x – X-coordinate of the vertex.

  • y – Y-coordinate of the vertex.

  • z – Z-coordinate of the vertex.

  • i – Structured I-index of the vertex.

  • j – Structured J-index of the vertex.

  • k – Structured K-index of the vertex.

property size: int

Parametric face size in index-space cells.

Computed as the product of the two non-constant index spans. For a fully 3-D range (no constant index) the product of all three spans is returned.

Returns:

The number of index-space cells covered by this face.

Set the parent block index for this face.

Parameters:

val – Zero-based block index.

set_face_id(val: int)[source]

Set the integer identifier for this face.

Parameters:

val – Face identifier.

normal(block) → ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]][source]

Compute the unnormalised geometric normal of this face.

Uses three corner points from the parent block to form two edge vectors and returns their cross product. The resulting vector is not unit-length.

Parameters:

block – The parent Block object whose X, Y, Z arrays are indexed by (I, J, K).

Returns:

A NumPy array of shape (3,) representing the face normal vector (unnormalised).

match_indices(f: Face) → List[List[int]][source]

Find matching vertex pairs between this face and another.

Vertices are matched by spatial proximity using a tolerance of 1e-6. Each vertex in self is matched to at most one vertex in f, and vice versa.

Parameters:

f – The other Face to compare against.

Returns:

A list of [i, j] pairs where i is the vertex index in self and j is the matching vertex index in f.

__eq__(f: object) → bool[source]

Test equality by block index and all six index-range bounds.

Parameters:

f – Another object to compare. Must be a Face.

Returns:

True if f is a Face with identical BlockIndex, IMIN…``KMAX``.

vertices_equals(f: Face) → bool[source]

Test whether all vertices of this face match another by coordinates.

Uses match_indices() with the default tolerance to check that every vertex in self has a spatial match in f.

Parameters:

f – The other Face to compare against.

Returns:

True if the number of matched vertex pairs equals nvertex.

__ne__(f: object) → bool[source]

Test inequality (inverse of __eq__()).

Parameters:

f – Another object to compare.

Returns:

True if self != f.

index_equals(f2: Face) → bool[source]

Test whether the six index-range bounds match exactly.

Unlike __eq__(), this does not compare blockIndex.

Parameters:

f2 – The other Face to compare against.

Returns:

True if IMIN…``KMAX`` are identical.

Return a hash based on the first and last vertex indices.

Returns:

An integer hash value derived from the (I, J, K) indices of the first and last stored vertices.

property diagonal_length: float

Euclidean distance between the two extreme corners.

Computes the distance between the vertex at (IMIN, JMIN, KMIN) and the vertex at (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX) in physical (x, y, z) space.

Returns:

The diagonal length as a float.

Get the two extreme-corner coordinates of this face.

Returns:

A 2-tuple of (x, y, z) tuples. The first element corresponds to the vertex at (IMIN, JMIN, KMIN) and the second to (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX).

is_connected(f: Face, tol: float = 1e-08) → bool[source]

Test connectivity by centroid proximity (legacy method).

This is a simple heuristic retained for backward compatibility. For robust contact detection, prefer touches() or touches_by_nodes().

Parameters:

  • f – The other Face to test against.

  • tol – Maximum Euclidean distance between centroids for the faces to be considered connected.

Returns:

True if the centroid-to-centroid distance is less than tol.

Translate the face vertices in-place.

Parameters:

  • dx – Translation along the X-axis.

  • dy – Translation along the Y-axis.

  • dz – Translation along the Z-axis.

overlap_fraction(f: Face, tol_angle_deg: float = 10.0, tol_plane_dist: float = 1e-06) → float[source]

Compute the fractional area overlap between two faces.

Projects both faces onto the dominant 2-D plane, clips the polygons using Sutherland-Hodgman, and returns the ratio of the intersection area to the smaller face area.

Faces whose normals differ by more than tol_angle_deg (parallel or anti-parallel) are treated as non-overlapping. A plane-distance check scaled by the characteristic face length is also applied.

Parameters:

  • f – The other Face to test overlap against.

  • tol_angle_deg – Maximum angle (in degrees) between the face normals for the faces to be considered coplanar.

  • tol_plane_dist – Absolute minimum tolerance for the plane-distance check. The effective tolerance is max(tol_plane_dist, 1e-6 * max(1.0, Lc)) where Lc is the average characteristic edge length.

Returns:

A float in [0.0, 1.0] representing the overlap fraction. Returns 0.0 when the faces are not coplanar or do not intersect.

touches(f: Face, tol_angle_deg: float = 10.0, tol_plane_dist: float = 1e-06, min_overlap_frac: float = 0.01) → bool[source]

Test whether two faces are in surface contact.

Two faces touch if they are nearly coplanar (normals parallel or anti-parallel within tol_angle_deg) and their projected area overlap fraction meets the min_overlap_frac threshold.

Parameters:

  • f – The other Face to test against.

  • tol_angle_deg – Maximum angular deviation (degrees) between normals.

  • tol_plane_dist – Plane-distance tolerance passed to overlap_fraction().

  • min_overlap_frac – Minimum overlap fraction (in [0, 1]) for the faces to be considered touching.

Returns:

True if the faces are in surface contact, False otherwise.

grid_points(block, stride_u: int = 1, stride_v: int = 1) → ndarray[source]

Extract all XYZ grid points on this face from a parent block.

Samples the structured face grid at the given strides in the two parametric directions. Only works for faces with a single constant index (const_type in {0, 1, 2}); for unstructured faces, falls back to the stored corner vertices.

Parameters:

  • block – The parent Block whose X, Y, Z arrays are indexed by (I, J, K).

  • stride_u – Sampling stride in the first parametric direction.

  • stride_v – Sampling stride in the second parametric direction.

Returns:

A NumPy array of shape (N, 3) containing the sampled (x, y, z) coordinates.

shared_point_fraction(other: Face, block_self, block_other, tol_xyz: float = 1e-08, stride_u: int = 1, stride_v: int = 1) → float[source]

Compute the fraction of coincident grid nodes between two faces.

Samples both faces from their respective parent blocks, quantizes the coordinates, and counts how many nodes coincide within tol_xyz.

Parameters:

  • other – The other Face to compare with.

  • block_self – Parent block for self.

  • block_other – Parent block for other.

  • tol_xyz – Spatial tolerance for node coincidence.

  • stride_u – Sampling stride in the first parametric direction.

  • stride_v – Sampling stride in the second parametric direction.

Returns:

(# coincident nodes) / min(N_self, N_other) as a float in [0.0, 1.0]. Returns 0.0 if either face has no points.

touches_by_nodes(other: Face, block_self, block_other, tol_xyz: float = 1e-08, min_shared_frac: float = 0.02, min_shared_abs: int = 4, stride_u: int = 1, stride_v: int = 1) → bool[source]

Test surface contact by counting shared structured grid nodes.

Two faces are considered in contact when they share at least min_shared_abs coincident nodes and at least min_shared_frac of the smaller face’s sampled nodes. This method is more robust than polygon overlap for detecting partial contact between blocks that truly share grid nodes.

Parameters:

  • other – The other Face to test against.

  • block_self – Parent block for self.

  • block_other – Parent block for other.

  • tol_xyz – Spatial tolerance for node coincidence.

  • min_shared_frac – Minimum fraction of the smaller face’s nodes that must coincide for contact to be detected.

  • min_shared_abs – Minimum absolute number of coincident nodes required.

  • stride_u – Sampling stride in the first parametric direction.

  • stride_v – Sampling stride in the second parametric direction.

Returns:

True if both the absolute and fractional thresholds are met, False otherwise.
